reason: B offers the more specific, testable, and physically grounded mechanism: SFE-mediated partial-dislocation activity and twinning can be correlated directly with strain hardening and fracture toughness against a defined Cantor-alloy baseline. Its main weakness is that compositional changes may affect toughness through variables besides SFE and some cited evidence is regime-irrelevant, but A is overly generic and assumes—without identifying an alloy or phase diagram—that a slight annealing-temperature increase will necessarily precipitate brittle phases rather than dissolve them.
